documents.title: EuroChip to Build New Fab in Saxony, Securing European Semiconductor Supply
documents.body: EuroChip, a leading manufacturer of advanced semiconductors, announced today it will construct a new fabrication plant in Saxony, Germany. The project, estimated to cost €3 billion, will receive significant financial backing from both the German state of Saxony and the European Union. The facility is expected to create over 2,000 high-skilled jobs and bolster Europe’s strategic independence in semiconductor production. Construction is slated to begin in early 2025, with initial output projected for 2028.

documents.body: European regulators have granted approval for Cablivi, a novel long-acting injectable medication designed to prevent HIV infection. The treatment, administered every eight weeks, offers a discreet and potentially more convenient alternative to daily oral pre-exposure prophylaxis. Initial rollout across EU member states is anticipated to begin by June, pending national implementation plans. Health officials hope Cablivi will expand access to PrEP and reduce new HIV transmissions.

documents.title: Lost Manuscript by Polish Romantic Poet Unearthed in Vienna
documents.body: A previously unknown collection of poems and prose has been discovered within the Austrian National Library’s extensive archives. The manuscript, attributed to a prominent figure of Polish Romanticism, was found misfiled amongst a larger donation of correspondence dating back to the late 1880s. Experts believe the writings offer fresh insight into the poet’s personal life and political views during a turbulent period of Polish history. Initial assessments suggest the work includes previously unrecorded odes and fragments of a novel.
